extracted.intended_audience: platform builders, preprint community organisers, scholarly-communication practitioners, and Crossref/metadata consumers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on aggregating, surfacing, and displaying community-led evaluations and curation of preprints, and on the metadata needed to support that work. Focuses on how a platform (Sciety) uses Crossref metadata and group/individual curation to improve discovery, trust, and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and trust in surfaced content
rubrics_metrics.description: Only surfacing the content they might be interested in and that they know they can trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sciety aims to make people more productive by showing users preprints that are relevant to them and carry trust signals. The platform surfaces content based on what users follow and the evaluations attached to items so that readers can find material both interesting and reliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-based curation and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors on Sciety are part of ‘groups’, representing organisations and other communities that facilitate some form of preprint evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups act as the unit of curation and evaluation (e.g., eLife, Biophysics Colab, MetaROR, Gigabyte). Platforms should allow groups to triage content, add reviews/endorsements, and attach group-level identity to those actions to communicate origin and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curation statements / review summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups provide some kind of review summary which Sciety shows as a ‘curation statement’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curation statements should summarise a review or endorsement, highlight specific strengths of a preprint, and reference updated versions when relevant. They serve as concise added-value content alongside the preprint to explain why readers should care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual curated lists and topic-focused collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals create their own highlights in lists which they curate by topic; for example, ‘preprints by authors in the Global South’ or ‘Papers we want to discuss in our lab’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms should support user-created lists and filters so individuals can surface papers by theme, geography, or other criteria. These lists are an additional layer of curation on top of group-based evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity feed visibility of added-value actions
rubrics_metrics.description: An update feed available to users helps them keep track of all the reviews and endorsements from the groups they follow; the activity feed shows added value in the form of comments, reviews and curation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a chronological or filtered feed of actions (comments, reviews, endorsements, list additions) so users can follow the evolution of attention around a preprint. Consider expanding the feed to show different forms of curation activity distinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provenance and transparency of who reviewed/curated
rubrics_metrics.description: By making this evaluation and curation activity visible, Sciety clarifies who has reviewed the work and which groups have added it to their lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display reviewer or curator identity (individual and group), and associate actions with their origin to provide signals of credibility and allow readers to weigh endorsements accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate types of 'review' in metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: There are so many things that are called a review, but in metadata, we know there are different terminologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and standardise different categories (e.g., comment, endorsement, full review, summary/curation statement) in preprint review metadata so downstream consumers can distinguish the nature and depth of evaluations. Work in the preprint review metadata group to develop recommendations and prototypes for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata completeness for discovery (front matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation of the papers that we could link to: titles, authors, abstracts, publication dates, and, to have a way to go from the DOI of a paper, a classic Crossref entry point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure basic front-matter metadata is present and accessible via APIs so platforms can display and link to preprints consistently without writing bespoke ingestion code for every server.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperable relationship metadata and versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace the relationships and the different versions of a paper across time (e.g., a preprint has a new version with a different DOI, or a preprint has become a journal article) along with dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture and surface relationship metadata so readers can see version history, conversions from preprint to journal article, and time intervals. Consistent relationship metadata enables tracing publication history across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for preprint version number
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where available, expose preprint version numbers so users can distinguish between multiple iterations of the same preprint. Note the practical challenge: not all preprint servers provide sustainable, standardised version-number metadata across the ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardise preprint-review metadata terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation and prototypes for more consistency in preprint review metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in community efforts (e.g., EMC Europe, ASAPbio, preprint review metadata group) to define consistent fields and controlled vocabularies for review type, authorship of reviews, group affiliation, and curation action, so data can be aggregated reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make publication-history relationships explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: Show if something has been a preprint, because it’s important to the authors, and it’s important to show the transparency in the journey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage publishers and platforms to link preprints to subsequent journal versions (and vice versa) via Crossref or equivalent metadata so the publication history is explicit and discoverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperability so other providers can ingest/surface evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Other providers ingest and surface this information on their own platforms, such as Europe PMC and bioRxiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish evaluation and curation metadata in machine-readable, standardised formats and APIs so third-party platforms can ingest those signals and surface them consistently in discovery tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational performance: API selection and caching
rubrics_metrics.description: Switched from public API to Metadata Plus for performance, and implemented caching (temporal local copies) to improve response times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For production platforms ingesting large volumes of metadata, choose APIs with suitable performance guarantees, implement caching (e.g., 24-hour caches) and local storage strategies to enable fast page composition and reduce load on upstream services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide added-value context explaining 'why this matters'
rubrics_metrics.description: Post these assessments and reviews alongside the preprint, which others can then use as an indicator of trust: why should one care about this particular study?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and curation statements should articulate the significance, specific strengths/limitations, and contextual relevance of a preprint to help readers quickly assess importance and trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage broader participation in public review and curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Trying to get more people involved in the public review and curation of preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design interfaces and incentives that lower barriers to contributing reviews, summaries, and curated lists; highlight contributions publicly to grow community involvement and the pool of evaluative signals.
